kind: Independent continuous complete one-second rAF callback count audit

method.event: render-loop rAF callback frameStart, not hardware presentation timestamp
method.reconstruction: N raw intervals -> N+1 known event times, t0=0, ti=cumulative sum; absolute t0=raw.previous-sum(intervals).
method.window: All complete (s,s+1000ms] within t0..tN; left excluded/right included; callback count divided by exactly 1 second.
method.minimum: Evaluate every valid left-exit event plus domain endpoints; independently direct-count every left-exit/right-entry breakpoint and all adjacent midpoints.
method.edges: Do not extrapolate or zero-pad unknown head/tail; 1 FPS integer quantization.
method.quantile: Sorted original values at floor(p*(N-1)), including GPU samples.
method.slow: Strictly >1000/60 ms; 16.667 is only a rounded label.
method.average: len(raw.frameIntervals)/recording elapsedSeconds, matching source; known-interval-span alternative retained.
method.gpu: Stats recomputed from raw.gpuTimes; queries cover samples, are not hardware present/cadence, and are fewer than rAF callbacks.

limits: Historical and final runs are different source iterations and dynamic cloud positions; no isolated optimization speedup is claimed.
Auto-scale run endpoints and governor events are available, but no per-frame scale trace or per-scale raw partition exists.
Complete one-second callback counts above 60 do not mean every frame meets 16.667ms.
These short local desktop runs do not guarantee 60fps on arbitrary hardware, OS load, angles or real phones.
The final auto run was pre-warmed at scale 0.78: equal endpoints and no new governor events, unlike the old scale 1->0.92 transition run.
Cloud positions/lighting differ across records, including final native versus auto; no isolated per-change speedup is inferred.
The seven previous datasets are retained as historical evidence; renamed files match the SHA256 from the previous report.
